newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Thai Airways plans new Hong Kong freighter link.
newsitem.headline: Thai Airways plans new Hong Kong freighter link.

text.p: Thai Airways International is awaiting permission to launch a scheduled freighter service between Bangkok and Hong Kong, the airline's cargo sales manager in Hong Kong, Roger Lee, told Reuters.

He said traffic rights are being negotiated and slot times at Hong Kong's Kai Tak airport are still awaited but the twice weekly service has already been included in Thai's summer schedule which begins at the end of next month.

The new service utilising a leased Boeing 747-200 aircraft is an extension of Thai's joint venture with Air France Cargo and Lufthansa Cargo, Lee said. One of the Hong Kong flights to Bangkok would carry on to Frankfurt and Paris, the other to Osaka and Los Angeles.
Thai, which does not have any of its own cargo aircraft, was operating a leased freighter service into Hong Kong until the end of last year but was stopped for unspecified reasons, Lee added.
"The new service is in the planning stage and traffic rights are still pending. I hope to have more details at the end of this month," Lee said in a telephone interview.

According to Hong Kong Civil Aviation Department statistics, Thai is by far the dominant cargo carrier of eight airlines on the Hong Kong to Bangkok sector. Latest figures for December 1996 show Thai carried 2,806 tonnes to and 1,313 tonnes from Bangkok.
The next biggest cargo carrier was Cathay Pacific Airways Limited with 910 tonnes ex Hong Kong and 797 tonnes ex Bangkok. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
